steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called **Rayleigh scattering**, in which sunlight interacts with gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere. Blue light has a shorter wavelength than other colors in the visible spectrum, causing it to scatter far more efficiently in all directions — roughly 5–10 times more than red light. When you look at any part of the sky away from the sun, your eyes receive this scattered blue light streaming in from across the atmosphere, making the sky appear blue.
